{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Support for a global climate change strategy based on technology-driven, market-based solutions.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for decreasing emissions, reducing greenhouse gasses, increasing energy efficiency, and mitigating the impact of climate change.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for maximizing any ancillary economic benefits from climate change.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The issue of climate change must become a global concern.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"It would be unrealistic and counterproductive to expect the U.S. to carry climate change burdens that are more appropriately shared by all.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"All developed and developing economies, particularly India and China, can make significant contributions to dealing with climate change.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Propose a Climate Prize for scientists who solve the challenges of climate change.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Honoraria of many millions of dollars would be a small price for technological developments that eliminate the need for gas-powered cars or abate atmospheric carbon.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Caution against doomsday climate change scenarios peddled by proponents of centralized command-and-control government.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[6]},{"claim_text":"Support for addressing the risk of climate change based on sound science without succumbing to no-growth radicalism.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[6]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```

```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Support for a global climate change strategy based on technology-driven, market-based solutions that will decrease emissions, reduce excess greenhouse gasses in the atmosphere, increase energy efficiency, mitigate the impact of climate change, and maximize any ancillary benefits climate change might offer for the economy.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The issue of climate change is global and must become a truly global concern.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"It would be unrealistic and counterproductive to expect the U.S. to carry burdens related to climate change which are more appropriately shared by all developed and developing economies.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"All developed and developing economies, particularly India and China, can make significant contributions in dealing with climate change.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Propose a Climate Prize for scientists who solve the challenges of climate change.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Honoraria of many millions of dollars would be a small price for technological developments that eliminate our need for gas-powered cars or abate atmospheric carbon.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Caution against doomsday climate change scenarios peddled by the aficionados of centralized command-and-control government.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[6]},{"claim_text":"Support for addressing the risk of climate change based on sound science without succumbing to the no-growth radicalism that treats climate questions as dogma rather than as situations to be managed responsibly.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[6]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
